title: Inside Isambard AI: The Infrastructure Behind Lumen Sovereign
summary: Cosine joined Lumen Sovereign coalition partners at Isambard-AI to see the infrastructure supporting UK ambitions and the engineering making it more sustainable.
body_markdown:
We recently visited Isambard-AI with our Lumen Sovereign coalition partners and members of the media, hosted by the[Bristol Centre for Supercomputing (BriCS)](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/research/centres/bristol-supercomputing/) and the University of Bristol. The visit brought us together to see the infrastructure, meet the people behind it, and understand what this national capability is already enabling.


Thank you to the BriCS and University of Bristol teams for welcoming us and sharing their expertise, and to our coalition partners for joining us.


Attendees learning about the engineering and expertise behind Isambard-AI.


## **From UK compute to sovereign capability**


Built on HPE Cray EX technology, Isambard-AI combines 5,448 NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips. Through the UK Government’s AI Research Resource (AIRR), Cosine has been allocated 500,000 GPU hours to train Lumen Sovereign on UK soil, supporting our work to build secure, frontier AI that organisations can deploy within their own sovereign environments.


[Our Lumen Sovereign coalition](https://cosine.sh/blog/building-lumen-sovereign-uk-industry-coalition) is helping shape the model’s use cases, security requirements, and governance standards for critical sectors, including defence, financial services, and healthcare. Lumen Sovereign is designed to run entirely within a customer’s own infrastructure, including fully air-gapped environments, with no external data transfer.


A closer look at the hardware powering the UK’s AI ambitions.


## **World-class capability engineered for efficiency**


The visit also highlighted how carefully that capability has been engineered around energy and water use.


Isambard-AI runs entirely on UK-sourced renewable energy. Its direct liquid-cooling system circulates coolant and water through a closed loop, carrying heat away from the computing hardware before cooling and recirculating the liquid. The supercomputer’s annual water use is less than that of approximately 21 average UK homes, or 1½ Olympic-sized swimming pools.


A particular thank you to HPE, who joined us as part of our coalition, and whose supercomputing and cooling technology is central to this energy-efficient design.


Building world-class AI means taking resource efficiency seriously alongside performance. Isambard-AI demonstrates how those priorities can be addressed together.


The cooling infrastructure behind Isambard-AI’s energy-efficient design.


## **A shared resource for UK innovation**


We also heard about the wider work taking place on Isambard-AI. Beyond sovereign language models, the facility supports research into personallised cancer vaccines, Alzheimer’s disease, air pollution forecasting, and AI safety. These projects show what talented teams can achieve with access to advanced compute, and why its value extends beyond any single model or application.


In conversations during our visit, coalition members and the Cosine team expressed a shared sense of optimism about the UK’s place in AI. Seeing the infrastructure first-hand, meeting the people behind it, and hearing about the work already underway made that ambition tangible. We left with greater confidence that the UK has the talent and, increasingly, the infrastructure to build genuinely capable AI. The opportunity now is to turn those foundations into lasting capability.


Thank you again to BriCS, the University of Bristol, and all the coalition members and media who joined us. Building sovereign AI depends on both infrastructure and collaboration. We’re grateful to the people making both possible.


[Learn more about our work on Lumen Sovereign](https://cosine.sh/lumen-sovereign) .
